x: Fred Denny and John Morris both retired in the first half of the race. Harry Shields " just out for a stroll" finally managed to beat second class standard by 5 secs. after 53 miles.

M.P.A.A. was held from Wimbledon on October 6th and Vaughan Thomas proved an easy winner of the scratch event in 39:02; John Knifton was 2nd in 39:46. Belgrave won the match 120 - 133 and Len Fairman (14 minutes) the handicap from Charlie Speechley (14:30) and Fred Denny (14:30).
BOTTOM RIGHT:John Morris receives refreshment from Fred Denny, with John Keown alongside.
FRED DENNY has also been in for a repair job. He is now back again at the roadside scrutinising the walkers' progression.

Chief Judge was our own GEORGE BENTLEY and amongst those judging were FRED DENNY - happily recovered from his operation, FRANK JARVIS who has also had a bout in hospital, evergreen HAROLD KING with SYD SPENCER, HARRY SHIELDS and BILL TRUE to cast their eagle eyes on the proceedings.
Congratulations to Fred Denny on becoming a Grade I Walking Judge, so that in addition to judging Club, Police and Opens Fred can now officiate at National Championships.

However a number of Belgravians were on the Officials List, and looking at the programme we find Fred Denny (Recorder) Jack and Joan Goswell (Results) John Keown (Judges Recorder) Ray Middleton (Chief Steward Refreshment Station) and Jean Middleton (Sales and Programmes).

Amongst the Judges were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Syd Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson. Ray Hall together with Fred and Bill were logging them in, the sheets going in to Jack Goswell and Frank Jarvis, assisted by their wives to get out the results.

Referee for the race was past President Ray Hall, whilst Chief Judge was Syd Spencer, also judging were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson, recording was Frank Webb and of course masterminding the final result in the back room was Jack Goswell ably assisted by Joan.

Amongst the judges were George Bentley, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Sid Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson and refereeing was Ray Hall. Again the course was changed using three laps of the hills using a less steep hill than previous.
